market_bullets: All 10 tracked tickers have October 30 notes. All ten frozen premarket snapshots are negative; nine Today calls are down and NVIDIA is flat-to-down.
Intel is the largest earnings dislocation: about -25% in its note snapshot, with server strength offset by the Q4 PC/revenue/margin reset. Arm and AMD also show severe red indications.
Every sampled VEL5 is positive, but eight RSI readings remain below 50. These October 29 completed-bar indicators exclude today’s gap and do not constitute a live bottom signal.
Amazon/AWS demand strength and maintained capital spending coexist with heavy funding needs. The notes distinguish monetized demand from externally financed infrastructure growth.
Upcoming company tests cluster around AMD November 3, Arm and Qualcomm November 4, Cloudflare November 5, and NVIDIA November 17; reporting evidence must resolve cash and margin uncertainty.
Silicon Motion alone retains a modest constructive monthly tilt; most monthly calls are neutral or defensive. Conditional longer-horizon upside is not a same-day buying signal.
Cash quality is a shared theme: inventory funding, accepted systems, customer collections, capex, stock issuance and FCF per diluted share matter more than product-announcement counts.
Calibration warns against celebrating wide-band containment as directional skill. Annual track records remain untested; all displayed bands are terminal-close scenarios, not intraday limits.
